title: Microsoft Purview: Teams DLP policies scoped to Microsoft 365 Groups extend to 1:1 and group chats
summary: The roadmap facts, licensing and documented control steps are supported, including the qualification that the PowerShell command edits the Teams inclusion list rather than selecting the Teams location. The checklist names controls missing from the table, and the OCR cost estimator should be labelled preview.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap plans to extend group-scoped Teams DLP protection to standard channel chats in other Microsoft 365 Groups.
claims.quote: This change will automatically extend the protection to standard/shared channels chats in other Microsfot 365 Groups and 1:1/n (non-channel) chats.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap plans to extend group-scoped Teams DLP protection to 1:1/n non-channel chats.
claims.quote: This change will automatically extend the protection to standard/shared channels chats in other Microsfot 365 Groups and 1:1/n (non-channel) chats.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The coverage extension is automatic, supporting defaultState on for existing group-scoped policies.
claims.quote: This change will automatically extend the protection to standard/shared channels chats in other Microsfot 365 Groups and 1:1/n (non-channel) chats.

claims.claim: The roadmap says adding users, security groups or other Microsoft 365 groups will no longer be necessary to protect these chats, subject to the OCR exception.
claims.quote: There is no longer a need to add users, security groups or other Microsoft 365 groups to protect these chats, except for customers that have enabled optical character recognition (OCR) in Teams chat.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Customers with OCR enabled in Teams chat remain an exception and still need explicit users or groups for this protection.
claims.quote: There is no longer a need to add users, security groups or other Microsoft 365 groups to protect these chats, except for customers that have enabled optical character recognition (OCR) in Teams chat.

claims.where: What's changing: third paragraph; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn already lists Microsoft 365 group scoping as protecting 1:1/n chats, unlike the roadmap's description of the planned extension.
claims.quote: | Microsoft 365 groups | 1:1/n chats | Yes |

claims.claim: Learn lists Microsoft 365 group scoping as protecting standard, private and shared channel messages.
claims.quote: | Microsoft 365 groups | Standard, private and shared channel messages | Yes |

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; rendered controls table
claims.claim: The existing-policy Teams location is reached through Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Policies > policy > Edit policy > Choose locations to apply the policy > Teams chat and channel messages.
claims.quote: Data loss prevention > Policies. Select a policy, and then choose Edit policy (the pencil icon). Navigate through the tool until you arrive at the Choose locations to apply the policy page. Select Teams chat and channel messages.

claims.claim: Set-DlpCompliancePolicy -Identity <policy> -AddTeamsLocation <value> modifies the identified policy's Teams inclusion list, as qualified by the row note.
claims.quote: The Identity parameter specifies the DLP policy that you want to modify. The AddTeamsLocation parameter specifies the accounts, distribution groups, or mail-enabled security groups to add to the list of included Teams chat and channel messages

claims.claim: AddTeamsLocation adds accounts, distribution groups or mail-enabled security groups when TeamsLocation is All, rather than selecting the Teams location in the wizard.
claims.quote: The AddTeamsLocation parameter specifies the accounts, distribution groups, or mail-enabled security groups to add to the list of included Teams chat and channel messages if you used the value All for the TeamsLocation parameter.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 group membership determines the users covered by this Teams policy scope.
claims.quote: Teams chat and channel messages ... Microsoft 365 groups (Group members only, not the group as an entity)

claims.claim: Cross-tenant chat enforcement follows the hosting tenant, so home-tenant policies do not automatically follow users into chats hosted by another tenant.
claims.quote: DLP policy enforcement in these cross-tenant conversations is based on the hosting tenant, which is the tenant that initiated the chat or thread. ... a user's home-tenant DLP policies don't automatically follow the user into a conversation hosted by another tenant.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Configured Teams DLP actions can automatically block sensitive messages.
claims.quote: messages with sensitive information that are sent to external users are deleted. However, your tenant must be the initiator of the chat or the thread. This happens automatically, and within seconds, according to how your DLP policy is configured.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Flagged or blocked messages generate a sender activity entry stating Your message has been blocked.
claims.quote: An Activity entry is also generated for the sender if the message sent matched a DLP policy. Flagged and blocked messages, activities are created stating "Your message has been blocked".

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Teams policy tips can offer an override where the policy allows one.
claims.quote: Notice that the sender can opt to override the policy or notify an admin to review and resolve the issue. ... You can choose to allow users in your organization to override a DLP policy.

claims.claim: Teams policy tips can offer the sender an option to notify an administrator.
claims.quote: The What can I do? Link opens a dialog box that provides options for the sender to resolve the issue. Notice that the sender can opt to override the policy or notify an admin to review and resolve the issue.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Learn advises allowing approximately one hour for Teams DLP policy changes to sync to user accounts.
claims.quote: Allow approximately one hour for your changes to work their way through your data center and sync to user accounts.

claims.claim: Changing the Teams location requires an assigned role with permission to edit DLP policies.
claims.quote: To perform this task, you must be assigned a role that has permissions to edit DLP policies. To learn more, see Permissions in the Microsoft Purview portal

claims.claim: OCR configuration requires membership of an applicable role group, including Compliance administrator.
claims.quote: The Compliance admin for your organization configures the OCR settings for your tenant. ... To create and deploy policies, your account must be a member of one of these role groups: ... Compliance administrator

claims.claim: Teams DLP is included in the qualifying licences, supporting the included licensing model for this scoping change.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) for Teams ... | Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) for Teams | Included |

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Teams DLP page states that support for DLP protection in Teams chat requires an E5 licence.
claims.quote: Support for DLP protection in Teams Chat requires an E5 license.

claims.claim: Newly covered users remain subject to the Teams chat DLP licensing requirement.
claims.quote: Support for DLP protection in Teams Chat requires an E5 license.

claims.claim: The cited Teams DLP page does not explain how licences are assessed for users newly covered by the scoping extension.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams DLP Microsoft 365 Groups scoping 401127 separate price rate licensing covered group members license. Opened https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-microsoft-teams; it states the E5 requirement but no assessment procedure for this extension.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: No separate price or rate for this group-scoping change is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Teams DLP Microsoft 365 groups scoping extension 401127 price meter OCR rate. Opened Teams DLP, Purview service description, OCR overview and Syntex Azure billing pages; none states a price specific to this scoping extension.

claims.claim: The roadmap item names no new meter or licence.
claims.quote: When scoping policies to Microsoft 365 Groups in Teams DLP policies ... This change will automatically extend the protection ... except for customers that have enabled optical character recognition (OCR) in Teams chat.

claims.claim: OCR scanning is optional.
claims.quote: OCR scanning is an optional feature that you must enable at the tenant level.

claims.claim: OCR scanning must be enabled at the tenant level and supports Teams.
claims.quote: OCR scanning is an optional feature that you must enable at the tenant level. After you enable it, select the locations where you want to scan images. You can scan images in Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, Windows, and macOS devices.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: second paragraph; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Using OCR requires an Azure pay-as-you-go subscription and incurs scanning charges.
claims.quote: To use OCR scanning, your organization's Global admin needs to verify that an Azure pay-as-you-go subscription is in place. ... Each image scanned counts as one transaction.

claims.claim: The OCR cost estimator can estimate scanning charges.
claims.quote: You can use the OCR cost estimator tool (preview) to estimate your optical character recognition (OCR) scanning costs. The tool scans your selected locations ... and projects how much OCR processing will cost before you enable it.
claims.fix: Change 'through the OCR cost estimator' to 'through the OCR cost estimator (preview)'. The preview designation is stated at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/ocr-cost-estimator.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes group-scoped Teams DLP policies, not policies scoped to individual users or security groups.
claims.quote: When scoping policies to Microsoft 365 Groups in Teams DLP policies ... There is no longer a need to add users, security groups or other Microsoft 365 groups to protect these chats

claims.claim: DLP simulation mode can be used to test Teams policy rules before enforcement.
claims.quote: use it to test changes to existing policies before enforcing those changes in production. ... For Exchange, Teams, Devices locations only items that are new during simulation are evaluated.

claims.claim: DLP alerts can be reviewed for Teams chat and channel policy violations.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview portal shows alerts for DLP policies that are enforced on the following workloads: ... Teams chat and channel messages

claims.claim: Activity explorer reports Teams chat and channel DLP policy matches.
claims.quote: Activity Explorer gathers DLP policy match events from Microsoft 365 workloads such as Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams chat and channels

claims.claim: This change concerns tenants with Teams policies scoped to Microsoft 365 Groups, rather than tenants without such policies.
claims.quote: When scoping policies to Microsoft 365 Groups in Teams DLP policies ... This change will automatically extend the protection

claims.claim: The checklist names OCR settings, simulation mode, DLP alerts and Activity explorer without corresponding controls-table rows.
claims.quote: 'Check whether OCR is enabled for Teams chat'; 'Test the rules ... in simulation'; 'Review DLP alerts and Activity explorer'. The only controls-table row is 'Whether a DLP policy applies to Teams chat and channel messages'.
claims.fix: The Before rollout steps checking OCR and using simulation mode, and the After rollout step reviewing DLP alerts and Activity explorer, have no corresponding controls-table rows. Do not treat the Teams location row as documenting those controls.
